text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Memo warns of cover-up in Nazi cases: Serious ramifications anticipated by Justice official's close relationship with Federal Court judge.
- Chretien rejects 50 percent plus 1 yes vote: Simple majority too slim for PM.
- Left leads in first round of French voting: Results show signs of discontent with Chirac's governing centre-right coalition.
- Iranian voters reject Muslim hard-liners: Win by moderate presidential candidate seen as call for fewer religious dictates.
- Ottawa, provinces consider single ID card: Proposed central data registry would pool information on recipients of social benefits nation-wide.
- Canada shines in global ratings: But still needs to promote its recently acknowledged competitiveness, observers say.
- U.S. banking reforms pressure Canada: Ottawa may have to review own bank laws; could face NAFTA challenge.

- U.S. casino operators faced with a risky business: Gaming houses are questioning their future as they deal with stiffer competition, saturated markets and deep-pocketed rivals ready to squeeze out smaller enterprises.
- Sherritt buys 'Cuba T-bills': The Toronto company has made loans of C$127 million to Fidel Castro's cash-strapped regime -- money analysts estimate is earning interest between 16 and 18 percent.
- Stock markets soar to record levels.
- De Guzman was not dying of hepatitis B - columnist.
- Unity, tax cuts seen as the top election issues.
